text: In the statue puzzle, Lumpl (the clay) can survive being squashed into a ball but Goliath (the statue) cannot. Applying the contrapositive of Leibniz's Law, this shows:
choices: Lumpl ≠ Goliath, so the clay constitutes but is not identical to the statue
the statue and the clay are strictly identical
explanation: Since Lumpl has a modal property (possibly survives flattening) that Goliath lacks, the contrapositive of Leibniz's Law yields Lumpl ≠ Goliath — 'constitution without identity.' This is the puzzle's standard reading; identity, rejecting the Law, or denying modal properties are the costly moves one adopts only to avoid the conclusion.
